questions.question: What color are warning signs with black lettering or symbols?

options.text: Warning
Service
Regulatory
Speed limit

questions.correctAnswerText: Warning
questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black lettering or symbols. They alert drivers to upcoming road conditions.

questions.question: What does eye contact with another driver mean?

options.text: Indicates that the driver sees you.
Doesn't mean that the driver will properly yield to you.
Guarantees that the other driver will properly yield to you.
May make the driver mad.

questions.correctAnswerText: Doesn't mean that the driver will properly yield to you.
questions.explanation: Eye contact does not mean the driver will yield to you. Drivers often look directly at motorcyclists but still fail to see them.

questions.question: Which one is NOT a safe way to prevent fatigue while riding?

options.text: Protecting yourself from the elements
Taking artificial stimulants
Limiting the distance ridden in one day
Taking frequent breaks

questions.correctAnswerText: Taking artificial stimulants
questions.explanation: Avoid artificial stimulants. When they wear off, they can be very dangerous. Instead, take frequent breaks, limit riding to six hours per day, dress to protect yourself from wind and rain, and rest when needed.

questions.question: When riding a motorcycle, what should you assume about other drivers?

options.text: Assume the motorcycle is as easy to see as other vehicles.
Assume other drivers can't see you.
Not be concerned with taking steps to ensure that other drivers see you.
Ride offensively.

questions.correctAnswerText: Assume other drivers can't see you.
questions.explanation: Motorcycles are small and have fewer lights than other vehicles. They are hard to see. For safety, ride defensively and assume other drivers do not see you.

questions.question: Why should you practice using convex mirrors if your motorcycle has them?

options.text: Most people aren't used to using mirrors.
Unlike flat mirrors, they make items look farther away than they really are.
Unlike flat mirrors, they make items look closer than they really are.
It can be difficult to remember to look at mirrors while riding.

questions.correctAnswerText: Unlike flat mirrors, they make items look farther away than they really are.
questions.explanation: Convex mirrors show a wider view of the road behind you, but they make objects seem farther away than they actually are. Practice using them so you understand how they work.

questions.question: When riding on a slippery surface, what should you do?

options.text: Increase your speed.
Make sudden moves.
Move to the edge of the road.
Ride in the tire tracks left by cars.

questions.correctAnswerText: Ride in the tire tracks left by cars.
questions.explanation: On slippery surfaces, slow down, avoid sudden moves, stay away from the road edge, and ride in the tire tracks left by other cars.

questions.question: What is true about brightly-colored helmets?

options.text: May make it easier for the wearer to be seen.
Can be distracting.
Don't help to improve a rider's visibility.
Are not permitted.

questions.correctAnswerText: May make it easier for the wearer to be seen.
questions.explanation: A brightly-colored helmet is recommended. It protects you in a crash and helps other road users see you.

questions.question: Why is a flat front tire especially dangerous?

options.text: It affects how you steer.
The front tire provides the power for the bike, so you will lose acceleration.
The flat tire will shake the bike, making it hard to use the mirrors.
You won't be able to use the brake.

questions.correctAnswerText: It affects how you steer.
questions.explanation: A flat front tire is dangerous because it affects your ability to steer. If your front tire goes flat while riding, safely exit the road as quickly as possible.

questions.question: What should you do at a blind intersection with a stop sign?

options.text: Stop at the stop sign then proceed through the intersection.
Ignore the stop sign and move forward to get a better look.
Stop at the stop sign before moving forward to improve their view of cross traffic.
Proceed through the intersection without stopping.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop at the stop sign before moving forward to improve their view of cross traffic.
questions.explanation: Stop at the stop sign first. Then move forward and stop again just before the cross traffic lane. Lean your body forward and look around obstacles to check for traffic. Keep your front wheel out of the crossroad while looking.

questions.question: What is true about a motorcycle windshield?

options.text: Is a good substitute for a face shield.
Does not completely protect your eyes from the wind.
Is required on all motorcycles.
Should be used on windy days.

questions.correctAnswerText: Does not completely protect your eyes from the wind.
questions.explanation: A windshield is not an adequate substitute for goggles or a face shield. Most windshields do not fully protect your eyes from wind.

questions.question: When stopping, what should you do?

options.text: Apply the rear brake first.
Apply the front brake first.
Apply both brakes at the same time.
Use only one brake, either front or rear.

questions.correctAnswerText: Apply both brakes at the same time.
questions.explanation: Use both brakes every time you slow down or stop. Apply them at the same time.

questions.question: How much stopping power does a motorcycle's front brake provide?

options.text: About 25 percent
About 50 percent
About 70 percent
About 95 percent

questions.correctAnswerText: About 70 percent
questions.explanation: The front brake is more powerful than the rear brake. It provides at least 70 percent of a motorcycle's total stopping power.

questions.question: When riding at night, how fast should you go?

options.text: Slower than you would during the day under the same conditions.
The same speed as you would during the day under the same conditions.
Faster than you would during the day under the same conditions.
On the shoulder of the road so other vehicles can see you.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slower than you would during the day under the same conditions.
questions.explanation: Ride slower at night than you would during the day under the same weather and traffic conditions. It is harder to see hazards in the dark, so going slower helps you avoid them.

questions.question: When is it most important to flash your brake light?

options.text: When passing another vehicle.
When you will slow down suddenly.
When there is a stop sign ahead.
When your signals do not work.

questions.correctAnswerText: When you will slow down suddenly.
questions.explanation: A motorcycle has one brake light, which is not as noticeable as a car's two brake lights. Flash your brake light to help others see it, especially when you need to slow down faster than expected.

questions.question: To make a quick stop on wet pavement, what should you do?

options.text: Use only the front brake.
Use only the rear brake.
Use both brakes.

questions.correctAnswerText: Use both brakes.
questions.explanation: Use both brakes if you need to make a quick stop on a slippery surface. The front brake is safe to use on a slippery surface if you apply it slowly to prevent it from locking.

questions.question: When should you increase your following distance?

options.text: When the pavement is dry.
When the pavement is wet.
When you can see through the vehicle ahead of you.
When the sun is out.

questions.correctAnswerText: When the pavement is wet.
questions.explanation: Keep extra distance between you and other vehicles if your motorcycle will take longer to stop. Increase your distance if the pavement is slippery, if you cannot see through the vehicle ahead, or if traffic is heavy.

questions.question: If your front wheel locks, what should you do?

options.text: Keep holding the brake until the skid stops.
Release the front brake and do not use it again.
Release the front brake and then squeeze it quickly.
Release the front brake right away and apply it smoothly again.

questions.correctAnswerText: Release the front brake right away and apply it smoothly again.
questions.explanation: If your front wheel locks, let go of the front brake immediately. Then apply the brake smoothly again.

questions.question: When you are about to pass another vehicle on the left, where should you ride in your lane?

options.text: The left side of the lane.
The center of the lane.
The right side of the lane.
Either the right or center of the lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: The left side of the lane.
questions.explanation: Ride in the left part of your lane when preparing to pass another vehicle on the left. This position gives you the best view of the passing lane.

questions.question: What should you do when changing lanes?

options.text: Signal, check your mirrors, and turn your head.
Signal and check your mirrors.
Turn your head and change lanes.
Signal and change lanes.

questions.correctAnswerText: Signal, check your mirrors, and turn your head.
questions.explanation: Always signal before turning or changing lanes. Check your mirrors and look over your shoulder to make sure it is safe to change lanes.

questions.question: When riding in a group, what should motorcyclists do about space cushions?

options.text: Do not need space cushions.
Should increase their space cushions.
Should reduce their usual space cushions by half.
Should keep an adequate space cushion.

questions.correctAnswerText: Should keep an adequate space cushion.
questions.explanation: When riding in a group, stay close together but keep enough space around each rider to be safe.

questions.question: How much following distance should you normally keep?

options.text: One second.
Two seconds.
Three seconds.
Four seconds.

questions.correctAnswerText: Two seconds.
questions.explanation: Keep at least two seconds of distance between you and the vehicle ahead in normal conditions. Increase this distance if conditions are poor.

questions.question: What can help if your drive chain slips?

options.text: Tightening the chain
Loosening the chain
Using the throttle more
Applying the rear brake

questions.correctAnswerText: Tightening the chain
questions.explanation: Tightening the chain may stop it from slipping. If tightening does not fix the problem, replace the chain before you ride again.

questions.question: Why should you check your motorcycle before riding?

options.text: Only a mechanic can check your motorcycle.
You should never check your motorcycle before a ride.
You should only check your motorcycle after a ride.
It helps you find mechanical problems or broken parts.

questions.correctAnswerText: It helps you find mechanical problems or broken parts.
questions.explanation: Check your motorcycle before every ride. This helps you find mechanical problems or broken parts that could hurt you.

questions.question: What is the best way to check tire pressure?

options.text: Look at the tire and guess.
Use a tire gauge.
Squeeze the tire with your hand.
Compare your tire height to another tire.

questions.correctAnswerText: Use a tire gauge.
questions.explanation: Always use a tire gauge to check pressure before each ride. A tire that is not fully inflated can still look fine, so you cannot rely on looking at it.

questions.question: What should you do if you cannot avoid a slippery road?

options.text: Lean into the slippery section to keep your balance.
Keep your speed to improve grip.
Do not worry about road conditions.
Keep your motorcycle straight and go slowly.

questions.correctAnswerText: Keep your motorcycle straight and go slowly.
questions.explanation: It is best to avoid slippery roads. If you cannot avoid one, keep your motorcycle straight and go as slowly as possible.

questions.question: Which factor does NOT affect blood alcohol concentration (BAC)?

options.text: The amount of alcohol consumed
How fast a person drinks
Body weight
Height

questions.correctAnswerText: Height
questions.explanation: BAC is affected by how much alcohol you drink, how fast you drink it, and your body weight. Height does not affect BAC.

questions.question: Why should you ride in the left part of your lane when passing?

options.text: It helps you see further ahead.
It makes it harder to see ahead.
It blocks your view of the vehicle ahead.
It lets the other driver go faster.

questions.correctAnswerText: It helps you see further ahead.
questions.explanation: Ride in the left part of your lane when passing. This helps you see ahead and makes other drivers see you better.

questions.question: Which of these does NOT help prevent serious injury?

options.text: A DOT-approved helmet.
Face or eye protection.
Ear buds.
Protective clothing.

questions.correctAnswerText: Ear buds.
questions.explanation: Wear a DOT-approved helmet, face or eye protection, a sturdy jacket and long pants, high boots, and durable gloves. Ear buds do not provide protection.

questions.question: How should a group pass another vehicle?

options.text: One rider passes completely before the next rider starts.
Several riders pass at the same time.
The last rider waves to signal no more motorcycles are coming.
Pass in a staggered formation.

questions.correctAnswerText: One rider passes completely before the next rider starts.
questions.explanation: Riders should pass one at a time. Each rider should finish passing and get back in formation before the next rider starts to pass.

questions.question: What happens to your stopping ability when turning?

options.text: There is less grip available for stopping.
There is more grip available for stopping.
Stopping is the same as on a straight road.
You should never try to stop while turning.

questions.correctAnswerText: There is less grip available for stopping.
questions.explanation: You can brake while turning, but you must be very careful. When your motorcycle is leaning to turn, some grip is used for turning. This leaves less grip available for stopping.
